papers.title: Quasi-abelian Cousin groups of number fields:a Galois-orbit criterion and the complete list
papers.abstract: Let K be a number field with at least one complex place. A choice S of one embedding K $\rightarrow$ C at each place embeds the ring of integers of K as a discrete subgroup of Cn, where n is the number of places of K. The quotient T\_K,S is a Cousin group, or a complex torus if K is totally imaginary. We determine exactly when T\_K,S is quasi-abelian. The answer is a Galois criterion: no complex conjugation of the Galois closure of K may interchange two of the chosen complex embeddings. Equivalently, S is lifted from a subfield with at most one complex place above each place of the largest totally real subfield of K. For totally imaginary K this is the theorem of Shimura and Taniyama on abelian varieties with complex multiplication; our results extend it to all number fields. We also obtain the rank of the N{\'e}ron--Severi group, and show that T\_K,S is either quasi-abelian or has only constant meromorphic functions.

papers.title: Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
papers.abstract: We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the generality of interface problems under consideration. To our knowledge, this careful analysis has not appeared in (nor does it follow easily from) literature published so far. Our explicit formulae directly lend themselves to explorations of solutions' qualitative properties such as regularity, asymptotic behavior and well-posedness. This work has also been of utility in the investigation of nonlinear counterparts as well as in the study of phase-transition phenomena, moving-interface and diffuse-interface problems. Such results for RAD and high-order PDEs will soon appear in a series of separate papers.

papers.title: Difference estimates for Chern connections on homolomorphic vector bundles
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the uniqueness issue of Chern connections from the Cheng-Yau type estimate point of view. We establish local difference estimates for Chern connections on holomorphic vector bundles over complete noncompact K\"{a}hler manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded from below. These local estimates not only enable us to obtain uniqueness results for Hermitian-Einstein connections on complete noncompact K\"{a}hler manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, but also apply to study the Liouville theorem for complex Monge-Amp\`{e}re equation on $\mathbb{C}^n$ as well as the Chern flatness and K\"{a}hlerness for Hermitian metrics on complete noncompact Ricci flat K\"{a}hler manifolds.

papers.title: Disc functionals and rational curves
papers.abstract: We prove a criterion for the existence of rational curves on compact K\"ahler manifolds using disc functionals. As applications, we obtain a transcendental version of the Miyaoka--Mori theorem with an optimal degree bound and a new proof of the characterization of uniruled compact K\"ahler manifolds.

papers.title: Harmonic functions near isolated subanalytic singularities: generalized horns and regular blow-up
papers.abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a subanalytic set of dimension $d\ge 2$, closed near $0$, with an isolated singularity at $0$ and connected link, whose regular part carries the induced Riemannian metric. We study harmonic functions on $X\setminus\{0\}$ near $0$. (i) If $X$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, for the intrinsic metric, to a generalized horn $\{(z^\gamma y,z):\ y\in L,\ z\ge 0\}$, with $\gamma\ge 1$ rational and $L$ compact, connected, subanalytic and analytic, then: - every bounded harmonic function extends continuously to $0$; - every positive harmonic function near $0$ can be written as $qG_X+u_b$, with $q\ge 0$, $u_b$ bounded and $G_X$ a fixed singular profile; - a B\^ocher-type theorem holds: a positive harmonic function is either bounded or tends to $+\infty$, and two divergent ones have a nontrivial linear combination that extends continuously. The proof relies on a volume doubling and weak Poincar\'e condition on intrinsic balls away from $0$, invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms, which together with an annular connectedness condition implies a Harnack inequality on annuli; the decomposition then follows from a Picard-principle argument whose geometric input is the Harnack inequality on the links. (ii) If $d\ge 3$ and the spherical blow-up of $X$ at $0$ is a regular manifold with boundary parametrizing $X$ near $0$ (condition (R) of the paper), the singular profile has a polyhomogeneous expansion, which is described and may contain a $\log\rho$ term, $\rho=|x|$. (iii) For the rotational cusps $|x|^2=z^m$, $m>2$, $d\ge 3$, whose spherical blow-up is not regular, the profile is radial of order $\rho^{1-m(d-1)/2}$, so that its exponent depends on the rate at which the sections shrink.

papers.title: Central limit theorem for energies of determinantal point processes on complex manifolds I
papers.abstract: We study the Bergman determinantal point process associated with a positive line bundle on a compact Riemann surface. Consider the U-statistic given by the Green function, called the Green energy. For a configuration of $N$ points, the expectation of Green energy is $\frac12 N\log N+O(N)$, and the variance is $(\log 2-\pi^2/24)N+O(\log^2 N)$. We prove a central limit theorem for the Green energy by combining local Bergman kernel asymptotics with an expansion for the cumulants. A central limit theorem also holds for the logarithmic energy of Bergman determinantal point process on complex manifolds.

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
papers.abstract: Let $\chi_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,\chi_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $\xi_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R$, we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2} \Phi_L(u) e^{izu} du, \] where $\Phi_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ \Phi_L(u) := \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \xi_L \left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu} ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $\xi_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $\Lambda_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge \Lambda_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $\Lambda_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $\Lambda_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $\Lambda_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $\Lambda_L\le95241/320000=0.297628125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.

papers.title: An extension of Janowski functions with applications
papers.abstract: Janowski functions are regular functions of the form $p(z)=1+p_1z+\cdots$, which are subordinate to $L_0(a,b:z)=(1+az)/(1+bz)$ for real numbers $a,b$ such that $-1\leq b<a\leq 1$. In this paper, we expand the space of the constants, $a$ and $b$, of the superordinate function, $L_0(a,b:z)$, to a larger set of complex numbers and provide some applications.

papers.title: Totally geodesic sets and Caratheodory geometry in the polydisk
papers.abstract: A subset $V$ of the polydisk ${\mathbb D}^N$ is called totally geodesic if every pair of points in $V$ lie on a Kobayashi geodesic of ${\mathbb D}^N$ that lies entirely in $V$. It is called a Caratheodory set if its intrinsic Caratheodory metric agrees with the Caratheodory metric inherited from ${\mathbb D}^N$. We prove that for algebraic subvarieties of the polydisk these two notions coincide, and we obtain a complete geometric classification of such sets. The invariant metric geometry of the polydisk is unexpectedly rigid: every such set is, up to automorphism, built from only two basic geometric objects: disks and a distinguished family of two-dimensional algebraic surfaces that we call Roman surfaces. Roman surfaces arise independently in the study of the three-point interpolation problem in the polydisk.

papers.title: Complex structures on products with $S^4$
papers.abstract: The main theorem of the present paper is that $S^4\times P$ admits a complex structure whenever $P$ is the fibre product, over a compact complex manifold, of the unit circle bundles of an even number of holomorphic line bundles. This theorem has lots of significant applications. For example, $S^4\times G$ admits a complex structure for every compact Lie group $G$ of even dimension. The same holds for $S^4\times V_{2s}(C^n)$ and $S^4\times V_{2s}(H^n)$ when $n\geq 2s\geq2$, and for $S^4\times V_{4s}(R^n)$ when $n\ge4s\ge4$. The theorem also gives complex structures on the product of $S^4$ with any even number of odd-dimensional spheres. Moreover, complex structures exist on $S^4$ times some moment-angle manifolds, including certain connected sums of sphere products. The construction uses a holomorphic $(C^*)^2$-action on $S^4 \times T^2$ endowed with the complex structure we constructed in [Gao-Tang-Yan, arXiv:2610.06067v1] and a smooth splitting equivariant under the compact torus.

papers.title: The $H^p$-Corona theorem on bounded pseudoconvex domains with $C^2$ boundary
papers.abstract: For $0<p\le2$, we solve the $H^p$-Corona problem on bounded pseudoconvex domains $\Omega\Subset\mathbb C^n$ with $C^2$ boundary, obtaining the bound $C_\Omega\delta^{-q-1}|\log\delta|$, where $q=\min\{n,m-1\}$ and $m$ is the number of generators. The range of $p$ is sharp even on a bounded smooth pseudoconvex domain admitting a smooth plurisubharmonic defining function and having only one weakly pseudoconvex boundary point.

papers.title: Complex Oscillation and Non-Oscillation Results of Second-Order Linear Differential Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate oscillation and non-oscillation results of second order differential equations \begin{equation} f''+(H_1e^z+H_2e^{\alpha z}+q)f=0,\tag{+} \end{equation} where $H_1,H_2\in\C\setminus\{0\}$, $0<\alpha<1$, and $q$ is an entire function of order less than $1$. First, we show that if equation (+) has a zero-free non-trivial entire solution, then either $\alpha=1/2$ or $\alpha=3/4$, which settles the Problem 9 posed in \cite{HITW}. Second, we prove that if either $q$ is transcendental, or $\alpha=(2m-1)/(2m)$ for some integer $m\geq 2$ and $q\equiv 0$, then every non-trivial entire solution $f$ of $(+)$ satisfies $\lambda(f)=\infty$.

papers.title: Hyperconvexity of pseudoconvex domains with continuous boundaries
papers.abstract: This is a reading note on a disc formula proof of hyperconvexity of bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$ with continuous boundaries.

papers.title: On the theorem of F. Riesz on Blaschke products and on inner functions in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^{n}
papers.abstract: For a convergent Blaschke product $f$ in the unit disc of $\mathbb C$, let $G(f)$ be the set of all points $t$ on the unit circle for which $|f(rt)| \rightarrow 1$ as $r \rightarrow 1$. By a classical F. Riesz theorem $G(f)$ is of full measure, which describes $G$ metrically. We describe $G$ topologically by proving that it is a $G_{\delta}$ set. The same description is true in general for inner functions not only in the unit disc but also in the unit ball of $\mathbb C^n$.

papers.title: Sharpness of the Brjuno Condition for Hyperbolic Bishop Surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $\mu \in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $|\mu|=1$, and assume that $\mu$ is not a root of unity and is not Brjuno. Let $Q_\gamma$ denote the Bishop quadric with $\gamma = 1/\sqrt{2+\mu+\mu^{-1}} > 1/2$. Gong and Stolovitch conjectured that there exists a real-analytic surface in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with Moser--Webster invariant $\mu$ that is formally but not holomorphically equivalent to $Q_\gamma$. We prove this conjecture.

papers.title: Nontrivial Expanding K\"ahler--Ricci Solitons and Automorphism Groups of Stein Domains
papers.abstract: We study complete nontrivial expanding K\"ahler--Ricci solitons with complete real holomorphic soliton fields. Let $\Omega$ be a relatively compact domain in a complex surface such that a neighborhood of $\overline{\Omega}$ admits a holomorphic immersion into Euclidean space. We prove that such a soliton exists if and only if $\Omega$ is Stein and the identity component of $\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega)$ is noncompact. On such a Stein domain, a complete real holomorphic vector field is the soliton field of a complete nontrivial expander if and only if its flow has noncompact closure in $\operatorname{Aut}(\Omega)$. In higher dimensions, we establish existence criteria using the adjoint representation of automorphism groups, boundary geometry, and homogeneous positive closed $(1,1)$-currents. We give sufficient conditions for the holomorphic $\mathbb{C}^{n-1}$-action on the universal globalization of a proper holomorphic $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$-action on a Stein $n$-manifold to be free and proper. Applications include bounded convex and homogeneous domains, domains satisfying weak Kobayashi visibility, and certain finite-type domains.

papers.title: Kushel--Tyaglov's problem, sharp Schoenberg-type inequalities and majorization relations between zeros and critical points
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a purely complex-analytic proof of Schoenberg's conjecture. We also determine the sharp constants in Schoenberg-type inequalities for every real exponent $p>0$ and every degree $n\ge2$, and characterize all corresponding extremal configurations. In particular, we confirm two conjectures posed in \cite{TZ25} and provide a complete solution to a problem of Kushel and Tyaglov. Furthermore, we introduce the tool of weighted weak majorization and establish, under the zero-centroid condition, new weak-majorization relations between the moduli of the critical points and those of the zeros. As consequences of these relations, we obtain refinements of several known results.

papers.title: Weighted Bergman projection in radial trees
papers.abstract: We study the Bergman projection $P_\omega $ on a radial tree with respect to weighted harmonic Bergman spaces $A^p_\omega $, where $\omega $ is a positive radial weight. We prove that for all such weights and $1<p<\infty $, the Bergman projection $P_\omega $ is bounded from $L^p(\omega) $ to $A^p_\omega $ and $L^\infty \to \mathcal{B} $, where $\mathcal{B} $ is the Bloch space of the tree. We also provide a characterization of the weights $\omega $ for which the positive Bergman projection $P_\omega^+ $ is bounded from $L^p(\omega) $ to $L^p(\omega) $. Finally, in the appendix, we provide an elementary proof of the characterization of the weights $\Omega \in L^1(\mathbb{D}) $ for which the Bergman projection from $L^p(\Omega) $ to the holomorphic Bergman space $A^p_\Omega(\mathbb{D}) $.

papers.title: Similarity preserving noncommutative maps
papers.abstract: In this note we study similarity preserving automorphisms of noncommutative (NC for short) balls. We show that every similarity preserving NC automorphism is, in fact, given by a similarity with an NC invertible function. As an application, we show that the group of automorphisms of the free semigroup algebra is generated by unitarily implemented and inner automorphisms.

papers.title: Quantum walks and conformal mappings
papers.abstract: We study the most elementary discrete model of an electron moving along a line, known as Feynman checkers, quantum walk, or the six-vertex model with special complex weights, and provide a uniform asymptotic formula for the wave function in the whole xt-plane. In addition to the well-known appearance of the Airy function that describes the transition between the oscillating and exponentially decaying regimes, we observe a second transition governed by the gamma function when the electron speed approaches the speed of light. We prove two general theorems producing uniform asymptotic formulae involving the Airy and gamma functions, using conformal mappings associated with the underlying integral representations. They are applicable in several other situations as well.

papers.title: Mahler's problem and Turyn polynomials
papers.abstract: Mahler's problem asks for the largest possible value of the Mahler measure, normalized by the $L_2$ norm, of a polynomial with $\pm1$ coefficients and large degree. We establish a new record value of approximately $0.951$ in this problem by analyzing certain Turyn polynomials, which are defined by cyclically shifting the coefficients of a Fekete polynomial by a prescribed amount. Recently, Klurman, Lamzouri, and Munsch established that the distribution of values over the unit circle of Fekete polynomials of large degree is effectively modeled by a particular random point process. We extend this analysis to the Turyn polynomials, and determine expressions for the asymptotic normalized Mahler measure of these polynomials, as well as for their normalized $L_q$ norms. We also describe a number of calculations on the corresponding random processes, which indicate that the Turyn polynomials where the shift is approximately $1/4$ of the length have Mahler measure exceeding $95\%$ of their $L_2$ norm. Further, we show that these asymptotic values are not disturbed by a small change to make polynomials having entirely $\pm1$ coefficients, which establishes the result on Mahler's problem. We also estimate that the limiting value of the normalized $L_1$ norm of these polynomials exceeds $0.977$, in connection with a question of Newman.

papers.title: Conformal tubular parameterization and toroidal bending of tube-like surfaces
papers.abstract: Tube-like surfaces are widely encountered in geometry processing, engineering structures, and medical anatomy, yet their intrinsic longitudinal and circumferential information is not well preserved by conventional planar annular or rectangular parameterization domains. In this work, we propose a new conformal parameterization framework for open tube-like surfaces with two boundary components. The proposed method first constructs a fixed-boundary tubular parameterization by cutting the input mesh, computing a disk-to-parallelogram quasi-conformal map, and lifting the result to a cylindrical surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$. To reduce residual distortion introduced near the cut seam, we further introduce a localized quasi-conformal correction scheme formulated on an annular domain, which improves conformality while leaving regions away from the seam unchanged. To handle noisy or irregular input boundaries, we also develop a free-boundary variant based on boundary extension and cycle-Laplacian smoothing, allowing the prescribed boundary constraints to be imposed on artificial outer rings rather than directly on the original surface. Finally, as an optional post-processing step, we derive two conformal toroidal bending maps that embed the tubular parameterization into toroidal geometries without altering its conformal structure. Experiments on synthetic tube meshes and real vascular surfaces demonstrate that the proposed framework produces low-distortion parameterizations, effectively mitigates seam-induced artifacts, improves robustness for boundary-noisy inputs, and provides flexible tubular and toroidal target domains for downstream surface processing tasks.

papers.title: Topology, Hyperbolicity, and the Shafarevich Conjecture for Complex Algebraic Varieties
papers.abstract: This survey presents recent developments concerning the Shafarevich conjecture, non-abelian Hodge theories, hyperbolicity, and the topology of complex algebraic varieties, as well as the interplay among these areas. More precisely, we present the main ideas and techniques involved in the linear versions of the following conjectures: the Shafarevich conjecture, the Chern-Hopf-Thurston conjecture, Koll\'ar's conjecture on the holomorphic Euler characteristic, the de Oliveira-Katzarkov-Ramachandran conjecture, and Campana's nilpotency conjecture. In addition, we discuss characterizations of the hyperbolicity of complex quasi-projective varieties via representations of their fundamental groups, together with the generalized Green-Griffiths-Lang conjecture in the presence of a big local system.

papers.title: Algebraic Dimension and Reduction of LVMB manifolds
papers.abstract: LVMB manifolds are a large class of compact complex manifolds constructed from an initial combinatorial datum. Most of them are non-algebraic manifolds nor do they support K\"ahler metrics. All LVMB manifolds are equipped with a canonical holomorphic foliation, whose leaf space is a complex toric quasifold; these spaces constitute the nonrational counterpart of compact toric orbifolds. For an LVMB manifold with no nonzero holomorphic 1-forms, we show that every meromorphic function is a rational function of the Laurent monomials arising from the rational linear relations among the points in the initial datum. It follows that Meersseman's lower bound for the algebraic dimension is attained and that the algebraic reduction is rational. In particular, both conclusions hold for every LVMB manifold with at most two indispensable indices. Under the same vanishing hypothesis, we relate the algebraic dimension of an LVMB manifold to the nonrationality degree of its canonical quasifold leaf space. We give an explicit formula for this invariant recently introduced by Battaglia and Prato.

papers.title: Resolving Gilbert's Conjecture: Dimensional Dependencies in Hardy Spaces Valued in Clifford Modules
papers.abstract: This article provides a thorough investigation into Gilbert's Conjecture, pertaining to Hardy spaces in the upper half-space valued in Clifford modules. We explore the conjecture proposed by Gilbert in 1991, which seeks to extend the classical principle of representing real $L^p$ functions on the real line as boundary values of Hardy holomorphic functions to higher-dimensional Euclidean spaces valued in any Clifford module. We present a complete resolution to this conjecture, demonstrating that its validity is contingent upon the dimension $n$, specifically holding true when \(n \not\equiv 6, 7 \mod 8\) and failing otherwise. The pivotal discovery that Gilbert's conjecture can be reformulated as a set of algebraic conditions is underscored in this work. To navigate these conditions, we employ a novel strategy that leverages the octonions, revealing their instrumental role in addressing issues related to Clifford modules and spinors. This innovative approach not only provides explicit realization through the generalization of the Hilbert transform to the Riesz transform but also establishes a significant advancement in the understanding of Hardy spaces within higher dimensions.

papers.title: On CR manifolds of CR dimension 1
papers.abstract: We classify all maximal symmetry models of CR dimension 1, depending on their Bloom-Graham and Tanaka types, give coordinate realization to some of those models and prove a general extension principle.

papers.title: The Schwarzian Derivative for Convex Holomorphic Mappings in Several Complex Variables
papers.abstract: We study the two components of Oda's Schwarzian derivative, the tensor $S_f$ and the quadratic form $S^0_f$, for convex holomorphic mappings of the polydisk and for Roper--Suffridge extensions of convex functions to the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^n$, with norms taken in the Bergman metric. For the polydisk we obtain the sharp bound $\|S_f\|\le\gamma_n$, where $\gamma_n$ is the maximum of an explicit quartic form on the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^n$, with $\gamma_2=2$ and $\gamma_n\to2\sqrt2$, and the sharp bound $\|S^0_f\|\le 4/(n+1)$, $n\ge2$, in both cases the extremal mappings are products of half-plane mappings. For Roper--Suffridge extensions both norms are computed exactly in terms of the Schwarzian derivative of the one-variable function. In particular $S^0_f$ reduces to the classical Schwarzian derivative, and the theorem of Chuaqui, Duren and Osgood yields the sharp bounds $\|S_f\|\le1/\sqrt{n+1}$ and $\|S^0_f\|\le 1/(n+1)$, with equality for the parallel strip.

papers.title: Composition operators and Rational Inner Functions on the bidisc: A geometric approach
papers.abstract: We study composition operators acting on the weighted Bergman spaces on the bidisc, i.e. $C_{\Phi}:A^2_{\beta}(\mathbb{D}^2)\to A^2_{\beta}(\mathbb{D}^2)$ where $\Phi$ is induced by rational inner functions (RIFs) or a RIF and a smooth function (mixed case). Our approach is geometric. Our main result is a uniform criterion for all $\beta\in(-1,0]$ that can be summarized as follows: Boundedness of the composition operator is equivalent to transversal intersection of the level sets for non-smooth symbols, under the assumption that if any tangential intersection occurs on the singularity it must be of high order. This extends the characterization of Bayart-Kosi\'nski to the non-smooth self maps of the bidisc. To reach our conclusions, we utilize results obtained by Anderson, Bergqvist, Bickel, Cima and Sola on Clark measures associated to RIFs and Puiseux factorizations.

papers.title: Landau-type theorems for $K$-quasiregular harmonic mappings
papers.abstract: In this paper, our aim is to establish several Landau-type theorems for $K$-quasiregular harmonic mappings $f=h+\overline{g}$ in the unit disk $\Bbb{D} = \{z\in\Bbb{C}: |z|<1\}$. Under various boundedness assumptions on the analytic part $h$, we obtain explicit univalence radii and corresponding schlicht disk radii that improve upon existing estimates in the literature. We also establish new Landau-type theorems under novel hypotheses. We provide examples to illustrate our results, and comprehensive numerical tables present quantitative values of the radii for various parameter choices, demonstrating the effectiveness of our results.

papers.title: Strictly paired ${\rm CR}$ linear automorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^4$
papers.abstract: This paper studies real-linear automorphisms of $\mathbb C^2$ through the ranks of their complex-linear and conjugate-linear blocks. Particular emphasis is placed on strictly paired CR (SPCR) automorphisms of $\mathbb R^4$, for which both blocks have rank $1$. Such a map is complex-linear on one complex line and conjugate-linear on a complementary complex line. Equivalently, the SPCR automorphisms form the double coset ${\rm GL}(2,\mathbb C)\,\sigma_0\,{\rm GL}(2,\mathbb C)$, where $\sigma_0(z_1,z_2)=(z_1,\bar z_2)$ is a mixed real-linear involution whose fixed locus is a real hypersurface. We show that the SPCR locus is a $12$-dimensional submanifold of $M_2(\mathbb C)^2$ and carries a CR structure of CR dimension $4$ and CR codimension $4$ on an explicit open dense subset. We also construct canonical diagonal and genuinely non-diagonal examples.
